subject: POC capacity planning with Aurora AI — success criteria & capacity proposal
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <priya@aurora.ai>, Joel Carter <joel.carter@aurora.ai>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — follow-up & capacity questions

Hi Priya / Joel —

Great conversation earlier — thanks for the time. Per the call, I wanted to capture the next steps and get alignment on the POC success criteria and capacity expectations so our infra team can prepare. Summary below, plus a couple of questions we need answered to finalize the POC capacity plan (attached draft).

POC goals / success criteria (from Aurora):
- Evaluate Redwood inference for Aurora’s real-time chat assistant on customer support transcripts.
- Maintain median response time < 150ms and 95th < 300ms for single-turn prompts (max 1k tokens).
- Ensure accuracy of model outputs vs. current rule-based baseline (support will provide eval prompts).

Questions for you (please confirm):
1) Peak concurrency for agent-facing usage during POC? (estimate of concurrent sessions / QPS)
2) Typical and max request token sizes (prompt + expected user tokens + max response).
3) Any data residency or VPC requirements for the trial?

Proposed Redwood capacity for initial POC (attached PDF):
- Reserved: 2 x A100-80GB equiv GPUs (dedicated pool) for baseline throughput
- Autoscale policy: allow burst up to 6 GPUs for traffic spikes; scale policy reactive + scheduled scaling (business hours 9am-6pm PT)
- KV/prefix caching enabled for repeated prefixes (expected 20% token savings per convo)

If you can reply with the concurrency and token sizes by EOD tomorrow, Lukas and Dev will size the exact batch/queue parameters and finalize the reservation. I’ve attached our draft capacity plan and your requirements spreadsheet — hope that helps.

Next steps:
- Aurora provides concurrency & token profiles (Priya) — due 2026-12-02
- Redwood finalizes capacity plan + pricing for reserved GPUs (Marissa/Lukas) — due 2026-12-03
- Schedule technical onboarding (Dev) — tentative 2026-12-07

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_poc_capacity_plan.pdf (1 page, high level sizing)
From: Priya Singh <priya@aurora.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Joel Carter <joel.carter@aurora.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — follow-up & capacity questions

Thanks Marissa — good recap. Quick answers below and I’ve attached our requirement sheet (filled).

Answers:
- Peak concurrency (expected during POC): 120 concurrent sessions, roughly 15 QPS sustained during business hours, spikes up to 35 QPS for 5–10 minute intervals.
- Token sizes: average prompt 220 tokens, expected response ~200 tokens; allow for up to 1,200 total tokens in worst-case (long context lookups).
- Data residency: must be hosted in US region; we do not need VPC for the POC but will evaluate for production.

Success criteria notes: we’ll run a 2-week evaluation with our labelled eval set (1,000 prompts) and compare F1 vs baseline and latency percentiles. If latency or accuracy is off, we’ll iterate on batching/quantization.

Thanks —
Priya
Head of Product, Aurora AI

Attachment: aurora_poc_requirements.xlsx (Spreadsheet — usage profiles + eval prompts)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <priya@aurora.ai>, Joel Carter <joel.carter@aurora.ai>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — follow-up & capacity questions

Perfect — thanks for the details, Priya. Based on the concurrency and token sizes you provided, Lukas and Dev put together an updated sizing + autoscale plan. High level: 

Updated proposal (initial POC 2 weeks):
- Reserved baseline: 4 x A100-80GB equiv GPUs (dedicated pool) — supports ~25 QPS sustained with KV caching and batching tuned for your profile.
- Autoscale burst: allow up to 10 GPUs for short spikes (up to 35 QPS), with a cooldown of 90s. We’ll cap burst billing to 48 GPU-hours per day for budget predictability.
- Throughput tuning: continuous batching (dynamic batch up to 32 requests where latency allows), token-parallel optimization for long contexts, and aggressive KV cache for repeated conversation prefixes.
- Expected latency: median ~110–140ms, 95th < 280ms (based on model profile we’ll use).
- Failure mode: automatic fallback to a smaller model (if latency SLO violated repeatedly) and cached-response degrade path.

Pricing/commit ask: to reserve 4 GPUs for 2 weeks we’ll include a trial discount on reserved capacity — details in the attached PDF.

Next internal items: Lukas / Dev — can you validate the GPU-hour cap and confirm the autoscale cooldown + batching defaults are safe for Aurora’s 1.2k token worst-case?

Marissa
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@aurora.ai>, Joel Carter <joel.carter@aurora.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — follow-up & capacity questions

Marissa / team —

Checked the numbers. Quick notes from infra sizing: 
- 4 x A100-80GB as reserved is a safe baseline for the stated 15 QPS sustained with 1.2k token worst-case, assuming KV cache hit rate >= 15% and dynamic batching enabled.
- Autoscale to 10 GPUs will handle the 35 QPS spikes, but we should set a per-GPU concurrent request cap (we recommend 24 concurrent streams per GPU for worst-case token lengths) to avoid OOM.
- Cooldown 90s is OK; I suggest we also add a minimum burst duration of 5 minutes to avoid rapid churn.
- Observability: we’ll wire up token-level breakdowns and per-route latency so Aurora can see 95th percentile in real time.

Action items assigned: 
- Dev: prepare the onboarding runbook & test harness (Dev will own load test scripts using Aurora’s eval set).
- Lukas: finalize autoscale policy and GPU reservation config; upload finalized plan to Drive.
- Marissa/Vivek: finalize the commercial (trial discount + GPU-hour cap).

I’ll push an updated redwood_poc_capacity_plan.pdf to the Drive link and mark the sections changed.

-Lukas
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@aurora.ai>, Joel Carter <joel.carter@aurora.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — follow-up & capacity questions

Quick status update — I ran a micro-benchmark with Aurora’s sample eval set (subset) against the proposed config: 4 reserved + burst to 10. Summary: 
- Sustained 15 QPS with 1.2k token window: median latency 125ms, 95th 260ms.
- Spike test to 35 QPS for 7 minutes: autoscale triggered to 9 GPUs, stable. Peak 95th ~ 310ms during scale-up window (we saw brief SLO transgressions during autoscale).
- Suggested tweak: pre-warm an extra GPU for scheduled peak windows (you can reserve 1 extra GPU as optional pre-warm during 9–11am PT).

I’ve attached the test logs and a brief runbook. I’ll be available for the onboarding call and will own the load tests.

- Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: dev_runbook_onboarding.md (runbook + sample harness), test_logs_20261203.txt

Date: 2026-12-03T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — follow-up & capacity questions — confirmed next steps

Thanks everyone — this is great momentum. Final notes and confirmed dates: 

Confirmed plan:
- Aurora provides full eval set + any gated prompts by 2026-12-04 (Priya)
- Redwood reserves 4 x A100-80GB for POC baseline (2026-12-07 through 2026-12-21) with autoscale to 10 GPUs and a 48 GPU-hour/day burst cap.
- Optional pre-warm 1 GPU 9–11am PT (enabled if Aurora confirms morning spikes).
- Dev to run onboarding load tests on 2026-12-07; invite for 9am PT technical onboarding call has been sent.
- Success criteria: match latency SLOs & meet accuracy delta vs baseline on the labelled set.

Commercials: Vivek / I will follow up with the trial terms and discount schedule (we’ll keep within the agreed per-day GPU-hour cap).

Thanks — looking forward to kickoff next week.

Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
